analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation-only: CHANGELOG.md has historical release-note text, and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md has a date bump plus a new 'Calibration ownership and foreground admission' section and a file-map row. No executable source or wire/protocol change was supplied, so I found no concrete security regression.

The doc describes provider-local calibration behavior:
- Calibration uses the engine's existing KV and service budgets and does not lower activation or OS reserves.
- One session runs per Mac.
- A customer request takes a foreground lease, cancels any current calibration, and waits for actual retirement before admission.
- Shutdown follows the same ownership boundary.
- Observations are staged per cell and published only after the completion posture check passes.
- The calibration health check is excluded from throughput learning and served-token totals.

Relevant threat IDs are T-010 (cancellation and DoS), T-028/T-029 (residual GPU memory and resource monopolization), T-041 (the prefix-cache oracle if calibration traffic touched the cache), A-001, and TB-007. The doc states no capacity wire fields or platform memory contract changed. I could not verify those claims against the referenced code: IdleCalibrationCoordinator.swift, EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibrationRequests.swift, and EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift. A later pass with those files should check three things:
- Calibration prompts must not donate to the SSD prefix cache, which would extend the T-041 at-rest and oracle surface.
- Foreground cancellation waits must be bounded, so a stuck probe cannot delay customer admission (T-010 availability) or extend past the request deadlines.
- Calibration prompts and outputs must not be logged or leaked.

The CHANGELOG text is historical and makes no new control claims.
